name: @attache/app
description: Attaché — an Envoy config workbench in the browser. Check a config, see what connects to what, and find out where a request actually goes. Run it with npx @attache/app.
author: Louis Emmett
//publishConfig: Scoped packages are RESTRICTED by default, and restricted publishing needs a paid npm plan — so without this the first release fails with a 402 that no dry run catches, because --dry-run never makes the access check. Set here rather than passed as --access public on the command line so that publishing by hand from a laptop cannot differ from publishing from CI.
//engines: A floor, not a support statement: the bin uses only node: specifiers, ?? and optional chaining. CI builds and tests on 24.
//files-og: The link-preview image is excluded from the tarball, not from the build. It exists for crawlers fetching the hosted page, and no crawler fetches localhost — so shipping it would put 82kB of social preview, nearly half the package, into a download whose entire pitch is that it is one small tarball. The Pages deploy uploads dist/ directly and is unaffected.

scripts.//og: Regenerates the link-preview image from public/og.svg. Deliberately NOT part of `build`: it needs rsvg-convert (brew install librsvg), which CI does not have and should not need — the PNG is committed, because a social preview that silently disappears when a toolchain is missing is worse than one checked into the repo.

//: No runtime dependencies, deliberately. What ships is a prebuilt dist/ with everything already bundled into it — React, CodeMirror, @attache/core and its `yaml` — and a bin that serves it using nothing but Node built-ins. So `npx @attache/app` downloads one small package and runs, instead of resolving an install tree first. That is the whole point of the npx route: somebody with a production config full of private keys should be able to get a local tool up in one command, without it going anywhere near a website.
//codemirror: The individual @codemirror/* packages, NOT the `codemirror` convenience bundle — that one pulls in search, bracket matching and a full keymap whether or not you use them. Measured before taking it: this set is 408kB raw but 115kB gzipped, roughly doubling the app to ~220kB on the wire, which is unremarkable for a developer tool. The deciding factor was not syntax highlighting, which is a 3kB tokeniser, but autocompletion: doing that on a textarea means caret pixel measurement, popup positioning, keyboard interception, and insertion that does not destroy the undo stack. @codemirror/commands is not optional — without history() the editor would lose undo, which the textarea gave us for free. @codemirror/lint was added later and carries the diagnostic underline, the gutter markers and the hover, all of which were otherwise going to be hand-rolled against the same DOM. @codemirror/autocomplete came last, and is the dependency that justified taking CodeMirror in the first place — so it is the one this set was always going to end up carrying. Together the two take it to ~239kB gzipped.
